title: Meaning first, the word last
statement: Introduce a new word by giving its meaning first and its label last, never by asking learners to guess what it means.
detail: A grade-3 reading rulebook's vocabulary routine orders each word meaning first, a description with the label at the end, before an example and non-example pair, the word's parts where it splits, and a say-it-back. A reading quality canon applied in a grade-5 audit adds that an unfamiliar word is never introduced with a guess-opener such as 'who can tell me what X means?'. The rulebook says it is grounded in BrainLifts on direct instruction, practice and knowledge and a reading-science corpus.
against: A later card design for the same course opens with the word itself, "1. **Word** — "Our word today is nursery. Listen to me say this word: nursery."" (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-vocab-design-2026-09-21/PETER-PAN-CARDS-SIX-BEATS.md`, line 13), and gives the meaning fourth, after the learner says the word and hears its parts.

evidence.quote: Per word, in order: MEANING FIRST (description → label at the END)
An unfamiliar word is never introduced with a guess-opener ("who can tell me what X means?").
BrainLifts (Direct Instruction, Practice, Curriculum & Knowledge), the reading-science corpus
